hooks.name: Postman Collection Sync
hooks.description: Production-grade Postman collection sync. Auto-scaffolds project config on first run. Deterministic, idempotent, spec-aware.

action.prompt:
An API source file was saved.

EARLY EXIT

Determine if the saved file contains API contract changes: route definitions, middleware affecting auth or request processing, request validation schemas, response DTOs, serializers or response transformers, path/query parameters, shared error handlers, or status code changes that alter the public endpoint behaviour.

Limit analysis to the saved file. Only inspect additional files if necessary to resolve routing relationships, middleware chains, or schema imports.

If no API contract changes are found, exit immediately.

SOURCE OF TRUTH

If the project uses OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, or any formal API specification as its canonical source, do not infer conflicting changes from source code. Report that sync should be driven from the spec and exit.

If the collection is generated by another tool or pipeline (generation comments, .generated markers, pipeline config, postman-codegen output), report that it is generated and do not edit directly.

Otherwise, treat source code as the source of truth.

COLLECTION DISCOVERY

Locate the project's Postman collection configuration:
1. Check for .postman.json in the nearest parent directory of the saved file (supports monorepos)
2. Fall back to .postman.json at the workspace/repository root
3. Stop at repository boundaries (.git, workspace root) — never traverse beyond the project

If multiple .postman.json files exist, use the one closest to the saved file.

FIRST-TIME SETUP

If no .postman.json exists and no collection is configured, offer to scaffold the project:
1. Ask the user for their preferred Postman workspace (or list available ones)
2. Analyze the project's API routes to determine folder structure, auth pattern, and variable needs
3. Create a collection following the postman-collection-standards steering file
4. Create .postman.json with the workspace/collection/environment IDs
5. Generate a project-specific steering file at .kiro/steering/postman-project.md with a version header and documenting:
   - Include at the top: version (start at 1), generated-by (Postman Collection Sync), last-updated (ISO date)
   - Collection name and workspace
   - Variable names and purposes
   - Folder structure matching the project's API domains
   - Auth flow (which request populates the token, which endpoints are public)
   - Any project-specific conventions discovered during analysis

If postman-project.md already exists, check its version header. If conventions have evolved (new folders, new variables, changed auth flow), increment the version and update the file. Never downgrade or lose manually added conventions.

After scaffolding, proceed with normal sync.

CHANGE DETECTION

Compare the current API surface against the collection. Only update if the API contract has changed: endpoints, HTTP methods, paths, path/query parameters, request body schemas, response shapes, serialization/transformation behaviour, authentication requirements, status codes, or content types.

Do NOT sync on: formatting, comments, internal refactoring, variable renames that don't affect the public API, logging changes, or test file modifications.

The synchronization must be idempotent. Repeated runs without contract changes must produce no modifications.

REQUEST MATCHING

Match source endpoints to collection requests using this precedence:
1. Explicit metadata mapping (if the project maintains source-to-request annotations or a mapping file)
2. HTTP method + normalized path (treat :id, {id}, <id>, [id] as equivalent path parameters)
3. Existing Postman request ID (stable identifier, more reliable than names)
4. Request name + folder context (least stable — names are often edited by humans)

If no deterministic match is found, report the ambiguity. Only create a new request when the endpoint is clearly new (no plausible match exists at any level). Never guess a match — duplicates are worse than a manual prompt.

CHANGE HANDLING

- New endpoints: add with docs and test scripts, using {{baseUrl}} for URL base, placed in the appropriate folder respecting existing ordering
- Modified endpoints: update in place, preserving request IDs, ordering, and identity
- Deleted endpoints: report and suggest removal — do not silently remove
- Renamed endpoints: update in place if identity is clear via method+path, otherwise report ambiguity
- Deprecated endpoints: mark in description as deprecated
- Versioned (e.g. /v1 to /v2): add new version, deprecate old — do not auto-delete

Batch related updates into one operation.

POSTMAN COLLECTION v2.1 COMPLIANCE

When creating or modifying requests:
- URL uses {{baseUrl}} as the host variable (not hardcoded domains)
- Auth inherits from parent folder/collection — do not repeat inherited auth on individual requests unless endpoint-specific auth explicitly differs
- Request body uses appropriate mode (raw/json, formdata, urlencoded) with correct Content-Type
- All variable references use Postman double-brace syntax: {{variableName}}
- Follow the postman-collection-standards steering file for quality standards
- Follow the postman-project steering file for project-specific conventions (if present)

PRESERVATION RULES

- Preserve collection-level and folder-level authentication — do not override inherited auth unless endpoint-specific auth changed
- Preserve existing request IDs — update in place, never delete+recreate
- Preserve request ordering unless new endpoints naturally belong elsewhere
- Only update examples that were previously generated by automation — never overwrite manually authored examples or documentation
- Preserve folders, tags, and organizational structure
- Never overwrite unrelated requests

SAFETY

- If a change cannot be mapped safely, report it instead of modifying
- Never infer endpoint behaviour that cannot be determined from the source code — report gaps instead of guessing
- Never guess. Never destroy. Preserve user work.

SUMMARY

Show a brief summary: what contract change was detected, what was synced, and anything needing manual attention.
